moments.alt: A grainy black-and-white satellite view of a Soviet coastline, with a red circle drawn around the airfield at Mys Shmidta.

moments.quote: Everyone went from an emotional high to an emotional low in about one microsecond.
moments.short: Everyone went from an emotional high to an emotional low in about one microsecond.

moments.quote: Instead the RV, because of a parachute failure, made a ballistic trajectory into the open seas, hitting with an impact of about 2600 g's at about 310 miles per hour.
moments.short: …hitting with an impact of about 2600 g's at about 310 miles per hour.

moments.alt: A white USAF C-119 banks low over the ocean, its trailing lines reaching down to a small parachute below it.

moments.quote: “Destroy the capsule!” So the capsule was literally beaten to pieces and dumped into the Santa Barbara channel.
moments.short: …So the capsule was literally beaten to pieces and dumped into the Santa Barbara channel.

moments.quote: One farmer had transformed the parachute lines into a harness for his horse.
moments.short: One farmer had transformed the parachute lines into a harness for his horse.

moments.quote: Fortunately, Discoverer-XIV yielded much more Soviet coverage than the total of all U-2 missions.
moments.short: Fortunately, Discoverer-XIV yielded much more Soviet coverage than the total of all U-2 missions.

moments.quote: (George Kucera, of Bissell’s staff, an inveterate cigar smoker, was inspired to select this name as he glanced at a cigar wrapper.)
moments.short: …an inveterate cigar smoker, was inspired to select this name as he glanced at a cigar wrapper.

moments.alt: Overhead view of a scorched launch pad: a wrecked tower labelled 'Damaged gantry service tower', black blast marks and a bright camera-flash glare at the center.
On the dark sea floor, a spool of film wrapped in torn plastic and crumpled gold foil sits half-buried in brown silt.
Two villagers in hats crouch beside the battered, hollowed-out capsule, one with his hands on its rim.
A rocket stands beside its launch tower, ignites in a cloud of exhaust and climbs straight up into a pale blue sky.
